Commentary.Commentary: Windies will rue the dropped chances as it's enabled the home side to score some valuable runs on top of that. Maybe they will be content on the whole with how they've fared overall, having first reduced the Tigers to 55/5, then taking the remaining 5 rather quickly this morning. Now, the visiting side has a big task on its head. Batting on this tricky surface won't be easy at all. The chase is on for sure. It's about to begin shortly.

So, in whose favour are the scales tipped? Difficult to say. The hosts would have liked to get close to 250, but a target of just over 200 isn't too bad either, given the nature of the wicket. Bangladesh lasted just under 19 overs, and scored 70 runs in that time. Bishoo was the star of this morning as he plucked three wickets, and Chase and Gabriel picked up the remaining two.

OUT! That's the end of that. Windies finally manage to bundle the Tigers out. Chase tosses it up on the stumps, Islam comes down the track and looks to go big downtown, but can only hit it as far as long on. Warrican there watches the ball carefully and gobbles it up. BANGLADESH ARE ALL OUT FOR 125 AND SET A TARGET OF 204!

We are ready to begin. Windies starting with spin straightaway, to nobody's surprise, as Jomel Warrican has the ball in his hands. Mushfiqur Rahim and Mehidy Hasan stride out to bat and the former will take strike. Two slips and a short leg in place. Here we go...

Hello and welcome for what could be the final day of the Test, if it plays out like it did on Day 2, that is. Bangladesh currently lead by 133 runs, which would be a good thing usually, but they've lost 5 wickets already. The surface is turning square and the spinners are running riot. But, in saying that, if they manage to cross the 200-mark, things would very much tip in their favour. Rahim and Mehidy are out there, and it's clear the onus lies on the former who see his team through to that point. Chase, Warrican and Bishoo have all chipped in with the wickets. It remains to be seen how this first hour of play goes, which will be most crucial for both sides.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

The day began with Bangladesh being bowled out for 324, and then the Tigers put in a spirited performance with the ball, wherein debutant Naeem Hasan took a 5-wicket haul. If it wasn't for Hetmyer and Dowrich, the tourists would have been in deep trouble. Instead, because of their attacking prowess and the backing of their bowlers, they are still in with a shot. If proceedings follow suit like today, then Day 3 could very well be the final day of this Test match. The action begins at 0930 local (0330 GMT). Join in for that. Cheers!

Bangladesh may have the slightest of edges, but in no way are Windies out of this game. After being bundled out for 246 in this final session itself, they came out firing and scalped 5 Bangladesh wickets to really peg them back. Chase and Warrican bagged 2, while Bishoo took 1 of his own. The wicket is turning and there's a lot of bite on it, which became the reason for the Bangladesh top order's undoing. Some rash choice of shots didn't aid them either.
He manages to survive. Bishoo bowls a quicker and a shorter delivery on the stumps, Mehidy Hasan goes deep inside the crease and blocks it under his nose. STUMPS ON DAY 2!
